mainTopic: Which מצוות are essential for יובל to take effect, and why the years of ערלה are counted from תשרי.
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the previous teaching: eating on ערב יום כיפור counts as if one fasted on both the ninth and the tenth. Then a ברייתא asks what makes יובל a real יובל. רבי יהודה says the year cannot be יובל without שילוח עבדים (freeing slaves). רבי יוסי says it cannot be יובל without תקיעת שופר (blowing the שופר). רבי יוסי gives two reasons: a שופר can always be blown, and blowing it is the job of the בית דין. רבי יהודה's reason is that the limiting word ״היא״ refers only to the phrase right before it, ״וקראתם דרור״, and דרור means freedom. רבי יוחנן adds that the חכמים say all three מצוות are essential. The גמרא then explains that the word ״יובל״ teaches that יובל applies outside ארץ ישראל, but only when it is in force in ארץ ישראל. Finally, the גמרא proves through a גזירה שוה that the years of ערלה are counted from תשרי. A ברייתא then teaches that planting at least thirty days before ראש השנה counts as a year.

steps.title: Eating on the ninth counts like fasting on the ninth and the tenth
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous teaching: whoever eats on ערב יום כיפור is treated as if he fasted on both the ninth and the tenth of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: …as if he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a teaching from the end of the previous section. Eating and drinking on the ninth of תשרי (ערב יום כיפור) is counted as if a person fasted on both the ninth and the tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of this teaching came on the previous amud, and here we only see its ending. The point is that the מצוה of eating on ערב יום כיפור is valued as highly as fasting itself. After this line the גמרא moves on to a brand-new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: He fasted
The ninth day (of תשרי, ערב יום כיפור)
The tenth day (of תשרי, יום כיפור)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not start a new idea. It is the end of a sentence that began on the previous amud, so do not try to read it as the start of the יובל discussion.

phrases.english: as though he fasted on the ninth and the tenth.
phrases.notes: End of the previous teaching about eating on ערב יום כיפור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous sugya, whose earlier part appears on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eating on ערב יום כיפור is credited as if one fasted on both the ninth and the tenth.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: freeing slaves is essential for יובל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ״יובל היא״. According to רבי יהודה, the year is still יובל without returning fields or blowing the שופר, but the limiting word ״היא״ means it is not יובל if slaves are not freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "It is a יובל" means it is יובל even if they did not return the fields, and even if they did not blow the שופר. You might think it is יובל even if they did not free the slaves. So the verse says "it" (היא) to limit. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about what makes יובל count. רבי יהודה says that returning fields and blowing the שופר are not essential, but freeing the slaves is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase ״יובל היא״ is read two ways. ״יובל״ includes cases where some מצוות were skipped and the year still counts. The extra word ״היא״ limits that, so one מצוה cannot be skipped. רבי יהודה says the one that cannot be skipped is שילוח עבדים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee, the 50th year
They released, meaning they returned fields to their original owners
They blew the שופר
They sent away, meaning they freed the slaves
"One might think… so the verse teaches" (the standard pattern for a limiting דרשה)

steps.confusionAlert: Saying the year is ״still יובל״ does not mean skipping those מצוות is allowed. It only means the other laws of יובל still apply even if those מצוות were not carried out.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "It is a Jubilee":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:10.

phrases.english: even though they did not release (the fields),
even though they did not blow (the shofar).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּחוּ —
phrases.english: One might think: even though they did not free (the slaves)?
Therefore the verse says: "it" (to limit),
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, continuing the chapter's discussion of יובל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, יובל still takes effect without returning fields or blowing the שופר, but not without freeing slaves.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: blowing the שופר is essential for יובל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads the same פסוק but switches the roles. Returning fields and freeing slaves are not essential, but blowing the שופר is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: "It is a יובל" means it is יובל even if they did not return the fields, and even if they did not free the slaves. You might think it is יובל even if they did not blow the שופר. So the verse says "it" (היא) to limit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי יהודה. Using the same פסוק, he says the מצוה that cannot be skipped is blowing the שופר, not freeing slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree on the method: ״יובל״ includes and ״היא״ limits. They only argue about which מצוה the limiting word protects. For רבי יוסי, freeing slaves now goes into the "not essential" list and תקיעת שופר becomes the one that holds the year in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
"It", read here as a limiting word

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the swap carefully. For רבי יהודה, freeing slaves is essential. For רבי יוסי, blowing the שופר is essential. Each puts the other's essential מצוה on the "not needed" list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: "It is a Jubilee":
even though they did not release (the fields),
even though they did not free (the slaves).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא תָּקְעוּ —
phrases.english: One might think: even though they did not blow (the shofar)?
Therefore the verse says: "it" (to limit).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה, using the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, יובל still takes effect without returning fields or freeing slaves, but not without blowing the שופר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks why he chose the שופר as the essential מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי asks himself: since one part of the פסוק includes and one part limits, what is my reason for saying freeing slaves is not needed but blowing the שופר is?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since one word of the verse includes and one word limits, why do I say "it is a יובל" even if they did not free the slaves, but there is no יובל unless they blew the שופר?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי asks a question to explain his own reasoning. This step sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself does not say which מצוה ״היא״ protects, so a reason is needed for choosing one over the other. The question shows that רבי יוסי's choice is not random. He is about to give a logical reason for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, given that
Includes (widens the law)
Excludes (narrows the law)
For what reason?
Unless

phrases.english: Now, since one verse includes,
phrases.notes: The word ״יובל״ is the one that includes, so those cases still count.

phrases.english: and one verse excludes,
phrases.notes: The word ״היא״ is the one that limits.

phrases.english: for what reason do I say:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹבֵל הִיא״ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּחוּ,
phrases.english: "It is a Jubilee" even though they did not free the slaves,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יוֹבֵל אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן תָּקְעוּ?
phrases.english: but there is no Jubilee unless they blew the shofar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁמִּקְרָא אֶחָד מְרַבֶּה, וּמִקְרָא אֶחָד מְמַעֵיט, מִפְּנֵי מָה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי begins to justify the ruling he gave in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What logic decides which מצוה the limiting word ״היא״ makes essential?

steps.title: There may be no slaves, but a שופר can always be blown
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers: the world can exist without any slaves to free, but it can never be impossible to blow a שופר. So the שופר must be the essential מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is possible for the world to be without freeing slaves, but it is impossible for the world to be without blowing the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his reason. A year might have no slaves to free, but the שופר can always be blown, so the שופר is the one that decides whether the year is יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An essential requirement has to be something that can always be done. If freeing slaves were essential, a year with no slaves could never become יובל, which makes no sense. A שופר is always available, so it is the fitting requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible for the world (to be without)
Freeing slaves
Blowing the שופר

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says the year is not יובל without freeing slaves. רבי יוסי says it is not יובל without blowing the שופר. רבי יוסי's reason is that a slave may not exist, but a שופר can always be blown.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבי יוסי's first reason. The next steps add a second reason (the שופר is the court's job) and explain why that second reason was needed.

phrases.english: Because it is possible for the world (to be)
without the freeing of slaves,
phrases.notes: There may simply be no slaves to free.

phrases.english: but it is impossible for the world (to be)
without the blowing of the shofar.
phrases.notes: A שופר can always be found.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא שִׁילּוּחַ עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The essential requirement must be something that is always possible. Freeing slaves may be impossible if there are no slaves, but blowing the שופר is always possible.

steps.title: A second reason: the שופר is the court's job
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds another reason. Blowing the שופר is handed to the בית דין, but freeing slaves is left to each private owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: this one (blowing the שופר) is given over to the court, and that one (freeing slaves) is not given over to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a second reason why the שופר, and not freeing slaves, is the essential part of יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית דין itself is in charge of blowing the שופר. Freeing slaves depends on each private owner. It makes sense that the essential part of יובל is the part the court controls, not the part left to individuals.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation; a second reason
Handed over to the court; the court's responsibility

phrases.english: Another explanation:
this (the shofar) is given over to the court,
phrases.notes: The court is obligated to blow the shofar.

phrases.english: and that (freeing slaves) is not given over to the court.
phrases.notes: It depends on each individual slave owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent answer to רבי יוסי's own question from step 4, next to the reason given in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שופר is the court's responsibility and freeing slaves is not, so the court-controlled מצוה is the essential one.

steps.title: Why was a second reason needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי added a second reason when he already gave one.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying 'another explanation'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי needed to add a second reason. This sets up the next step, which explains the gap in the first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one good reason is enough. If רבי יוסי gave two, the first one must have a weak spot that the second one covers.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the point?

phrases.english: What is the point of "another explanation"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 6 adds a second reason on top of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first reason (a world without slaves) was not enough by itself.

steps.title: In case someone rejects the first reason
steps.stepSummary: Someone might argue that somewhere in the world there will always be at least one slave owner. The second reason still works even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: it is impossible that there will not be even one person at the end of the world who does not free (his slaves), then still: this (the שופר) is given over to the court, and that (freeing slaves) is not given over to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second reason covers a possible weakness in the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason said a world with no slaves is possible. Someone could argue that somewhere, even at the far end of the world, there will always be a slave to free, so that reason falls away. The second reason, that the court controls the שופר, does not depend on that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; in case you argue
It is impossible
The end of the world; the farthest place
Sends away; frees (slaves)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
it is impossible that there is not even one
at the end of the world who does not free (his slaves),
phrases.notes: Meaning: there will always be some slave owner somewhere, so slaves will always be freed.

phrases.english: then still, this (the shofar) is given over to the court,
and that (freeing slaves) is not given over to the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by showing that the second reason still holds if the first reason is rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second reason is a backup in case someone claims there will always be slaves somewhere, which would weaken the first reason.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי has two reasons the שופר is essential: (1) there can be a world without slaves, but never one where a שופר cannot be blown; (2) the שופר is the court's job, while freeing slaves is up to private owners.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explained himself. The גמרא now asks why רבי יהודה says freeing slaves is the essential part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יוסי, since he stated his reason. But for רבי יהודה, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side and asks for רבי יהודה's source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי explained why he connects the limiting word ״היא״ to the שופר. רבי יהודה connects it to freeing slaves, but the ברייתא did not give his reason. The גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it works well (for one side, but...)
But (introducing the side that is harder to explain)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yosei,
since he stated his reason,
but according to Rabbi Yehuda, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי כִּדְקָאָמַר טַעְמֵיהּ, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי's reasoning back to רבי יהודה's view from step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה ties the limiting word ״היא״ to freeing slaves and not to the שופר.

steps.title: The limiting word refers only to the clause right before it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a word in the פסוק explains only the phrase directly before it. Right before ״היא״ the פסוק says ״וקראתם דרור״, which is about freeing slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land.' And he (רבי יהודה) holds that a פסוק is explained by what comes right before it, and not by what comes before that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהודה's reason. The limiting word is attached to the phrase closest to it, which is about freeing slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase directly before the limiting word is ״וקראתם דרור בארץ״, proclaiming freedom for slaves. The שופר is mentioned earlier, in the previous פסוק. Since רבי יהודה reads a word only with the clause right before it, the limit applies to freeing slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall proclaim liberty
He holds; his view is

keyTerms.term: מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ לְפָנָיו וְלֹא לִפְנֵי פָנָיו
keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק is explained by what is right before it, not by what is two steps before

steps.confusionAlert: ״לפניו״ here means 'the phrase right before it,' and ״לפני פניו״ means 'the phrase before that one.' It is about distance in the text, not about time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of how to read פסוקים: a limiting word attaches to the nearest clause. It is the real root of the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land,"
phrases.notes: This comes immediately before "it shall be a Jubilee."

phrases.english: and he holds: a verse is expounded with what is right before it,
and not with what comes before that.
phrases.notes: The shofar is mentioned further back, so the limit does not reach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by giving רבי יהודה's source and his rule for reading the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting word applies only to the clause right before it, ״וקראתם דרור״, which is about freeing slaves.

steps.title: How do we know דרור means freedom?
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that דרור means freedom. The גמרא asks where we learn that.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to everyone, דרור means freedom. From where is this understood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source that the word דרור means freedom. This sets up the proof from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's reading depends on ״וקראתם דרור״ being about freeing slaves. Both sides seem to agree on that meaning, so the גמרא asks how we know it.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone
A word meaning freedom
From where is this understood? What shows it?

phrases.english: According to everyone, "deror" is a term meaning liberty;
from where is this understood?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in step 10's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that דרור means freedom.

steps.title: A ברייתא: דרור only means freedom
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the word דרור means nothing other than freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: דרור means only freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that defines דרור as freedom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that ״וקראתם דרור״ is about setting people free. That supports reading the clause as freeing slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Is nothing other than; means only

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"Deror" is a term meaning only liberty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא states that דרור means only freedom.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains the word דרור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that דרור describes a person who can live anywhere and trade anywhere, completely free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: What is the meaning of the word דרור? It is like a person who lives in any dwelling he wants and moves merchandise through the whole country.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה shows how the word דרור carries the meaning of freedom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה links דרור to the root for dwelling (מדייר, דיירא). A free person can live wherever he likes and do business anywhere. That is exactly what a freed slave gains.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dwells; lives
Any dwelling place
Moves merchandise; does business
Throughout the whole country

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה makes freeing slaves essential to יובל because the limiting word applies only to the nearest clause, ״וקראתם דרור״, and דרור means freedom: the freedom to live and trade anywhere.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
What is the meaning of the word "deror"?
It is like one who dwells in any dwelling,
phrases.notes: A wordplay connecting דרור to דייר (dwelling).

phrases.english: and moves merchandise throughout the entire country.
phrases.notes: He is free to live and do business wherever he wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מָה לְשׁוֹן דְּרוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 12, adding רבי יהודה's explanation of the word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דרור means the freedom to live anywhere and trade anywhere.

steps.title: The חכמים say all three parts of יובל are required
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי is only their opinion. The חכמים say all three parts of יובל are essential, because a פסוק can be explained in light of the phrases before it and after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: That is the view of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. But the חכמים say all three things are required for יובל. They hold that a פסוק is explained in light of the phrase right before it, the phrase before that, and the phrase after it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion comes in. The חכמים disagree with both רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי and say that all three parts of יובל are required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה linked the limiting word ״היא״ only to the phrase right before it, which is freeing slaves. The חכמים let ״היא״ apply to every phrase around it: freeing slaves, blowing the שופר, and releasing land. So if any one of the three is missing, the year is not יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view
All three of them
Hold it back; essential, so it cannot happen without them
A verse is explained in light of what comes before it
And in light of what comes after it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views. רבי יהודה says freeing slaves is essential. רבי יוסי says blowing the שופר is essential. The חכמים say all three are essential.
steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement is not about whether these three things are מצוות of יובל. Everyone agrees they are. The question is which of them is so essential that the year is not יובל without it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: This is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei.
But the Sages say:
All three of them are essential to it.
phrases.notes: The three are releasing land, blowing the shofar, and freeing slaves.

phrases.english: They hold: a verse is explained in light of what is right before it,
and what is before that, and what comes after it.

steps.title: The word ״יובל״ seems to include even an incomplete year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the חכמים: the word ״יובל״ seems to mean it is יובל no matter what.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written ״יובל״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view of the חכמים using another word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״היא״ limits יובל to years where all three parts happen. The extra word ״יובל״ seems to include more cases, so it should cancel out that limit. That would mean the year is יובל even if some parts are missing.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (an opening for a challenge)

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״יובל״ includes more cases and should cancel out the limiting word ״היא״.

steps.title: ״יובל״ teaches that it applies even outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The word ״יובל״ is used for a different lesson: יובל applies even in חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches that it applies even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving the word ״יובל״ a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״יובל״ is not there to cancel the limit of ״היא״. It teaches where יובל applies: outside the Land too. Since that word is already used for this, the view of the חכמים still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That one, meaning that word is used for something else
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: That word teaches that it applies even outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different use
steps.terutzMaskana: ״יובל״ teaches that יובל applies even outside the Land

steps.title: But the verse says 'in the land'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer: the פסוק says ״בארץ״, which suggests יובל applies only in the Land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written ״בארץ״, "in the land"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave, that יובל applies outside the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says freedom is proclaimed ״בארץ״, in the land. That sounds like יובל is limited to ארץ ישראל. This seems to contradict the lesson that it applies in חוץ לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: In the land

phrases.english: But it is written: "In the land"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יובל applies outside the Land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ״בארץ״ seems to limit יובל to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Outside the Land follows the Land
steps.stepSummary: ״בארץ״ means that יובל applies in חוץ לארץ only when it is in force in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches: when freeing slaves is in force in the Land, it is also in force outside the Land. When it is not in force in the Land, it is not in force outside the Land either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two words work together. ״בארץ״ makes the outside depend on the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״יובל״ extends the law outside the Land. ״בארץ״ sets the condition: that only happens when יובל is in force in ארץ ישראל. So the words do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time when it is in force
Freedom, here the freeing of slaves

steps.whatToRemember: יובל applies outside the Land, but only during the times it is in force in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: That word teaches: when freedom is in force in the Land,

When it is not in force in the Land,
it is not in force outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word gets its own job, so they fit together
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בארץ″ limits יובל to the Land only
steps.terutzMaskana: Outside the Land follows the Land

steps.title: Source for תשרי as the new year for planting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for the source that א׳ תשרי is the new year for planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says "and for planting." From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule about planting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees are counted in years for ערלה, the first three years when their fruit is forbidden. The משנה says those years start counting from תשרי. The גמרא wants to know how we know that.

keyTerms.meaning: Planting, meaning counting a tree's years

steps.title: Learning 'year' from 'year' in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The ערלה verses use the word ״שנה״. A גזירה שוה links them to ״מראשית השנה״, which refers to תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says "three years they shall be ערלה," and it says "and in the fourth year." We learn the word ״שנה״ from ״שנה״ in a verse about תשרי, as it says: "from the beginning of the year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source using a גזירה שוה, which links two verses that use the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערלה verses count years, but they do not say when a year starts. The verse ״מראשית השנה״ also uses the word ״שנה״, and it refers to a year that starts in תשרי. Because the same word appears in both places, the ערלה years also start from תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fruit of a tree's first three years (ערלה)

steps.title: Why not learn 'year' from ניסן instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't learn ״שנה״ from the verse about ניסן, ״ראשון הוא לכם לחדשי השנה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn ״שנה״ from ״שנה״ from ניסן instead, as it says: "It shall be the first for you of the months of the year."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison by pointing to another verse with the same word that points to ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״שנה״ also appears in the ניסן verse. So the same kind of comparison could make the ערלה years start in ניסן. Why choose תשרי?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn instead
The month of Nisan

steps.title: Compare 'year' without months to 'year' without months
steps.stepSummary: The ערלה verse and the תשרי verse both say ״שנה״ with no mention of months. The ניסן verse mentions months, so it is not as close a match.
steps.simpleTranslation: We compare a "year" with no months mentioned to a "year" with no months mentioned. We do not compare a "year" with no months mentioned to a "year" that has months mentioned with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תשרי verse is the closer match, so that is the one we compare to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״שלש שנים״ and ״מראשית השנה״ both mention ״שנה״ alone. The ניסן verse speaks of the months of the year, which is a different setting. We always compare to the closest match, so the ערלה years start from תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or compare
Months
That does not have with it

steps.whatToRemember: The years of ערלה are counted from תשרי. The ערלה verse matches ״מראשית השנה״, where ״שנה״ stands alone, and not the ניסן verse, which talks about months.

steps.title: Planting thirty days before ראש השנה counts as a year
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that planting, layering, or grafting at least thirty days before ראש השנה of the שביעית year counts as one year for ערלה, and the plant may be kept during שביעית. With less than thirty days, it does not count as a year, and the plant may not be kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone may plant a tree, bend a vine branch into the ground so it takes root, or graft a branch onto a tree, on ערב שביעית. If he did it thirty days before ראש השנה, a year is counted for him, and he may keep the plants during שביעית. If he did it less than thirty days before ראש השנה, a year is not counted for him, and he may not keep the plants during שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that applies the rule that א׳ תשרי is the new year for planting. It tells us how close to ראש השנה you can plant and still have it count as a year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree needs about thirty days to take root. If it took root before ראש השנה, its first ערלה year ends on ראש השנה, even though only about a month has passed. If it has not had thirty days, it is treated as if it was planted in the new year. That affects ערלה, and it also means that keeping it in the ground during שביעית looks like planting in שביעית, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Layering: bending a vine branch into the ground so it roots as a new plant
Grafting: attaching a branch from one tree onto another
The year just before the Sabbatical year
"A year is counted for him": the time counts as a full year toward ערלה
To keep the plants alive and in the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Thirty days before ראש השנה is the key line. With thirty days, the plant counts one ערלה year at ראש השנה and may stay during שביעית. With less, there is no year counted and it may not stay.
steps.confusionAlert: "A year is counted" does not mean thirty days equals a year in general. It means the tree's first year ends at ראש השנה, because the new year for planting is תשרי. The thirty days are needed only so the tree has taken root before that date.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the practical result of the earlier proof that תשרי is the new year for planting. It also sets up the next questions in the גמרא about where the thirty-day number comes from.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting, layering, or grafting at least thirty days before ראש השנה counts as a year for ערלה, and the plant may be kept in שביעית. With less than thirty days, no year is counted, and keeping the plant in שביעית is forbidden.
